checks.detail: robots.txt is served, but named AI agents are refused: GPTBot restricted, ClaudeBot restricted, CCBot restricted, Google-Extended restricted.
/llms.txt served as genuine text (28658 bytes captured).
Sitemap served as XML — agents can enumerate public content without scraping.
Homepage carries no RSS/Atom <link rel="alternate"> discovery tag.
A developer portal page serves, but no machine-readable API spec was discovered.
No Web Bot Auth key directory published (status 404) — the site gives signed agents no way to be recognized. Expected almost everywhere today; recorded as data.

fixes: Publish/maintain /robots.txt and scope any Disallow rules to the paths that need them; a blanket block of named AI agents also blocks the agents your own users send.
Add <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml"> (or Atom) discovery tags to the homepage, or publish a feed — feeds are the lowest-cost agent channel there is.
Publish a machine-readable API surface: an OpenAPI document (conventionally /openapi.json) or a documented /api — agents integrate against specs, not markup.

Publish your Web Bot Auth key directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory and, on the receiving side, exempt verified signed agents from managed challenges on public paths (authenticated paths keep full protection).
